wins.text: Firm reported net income of $14.4B and EPS of $5.07 with ROTCE of 20%; revenue of $47.1B was up 9% YoY
CIB revenue of $19.9B up 17% YoY; Equities up 33% YoY and Fixed Income up 21% YoY on robust client activity; IB fees up 16% YoY with particular strength in equity underwriting
AWM reported record revenue of $6.1B up 12% YoY; AUM of $4.6T up 18% YoY; client assets of $6.8T up 20% YoY; long-term net inflows of $72B in the quarter
CCB retained #1 position in retail deposit share for fifth consecutive year; best year ever for new Sapphire account acquisitions; over 400,000 net new checking accounts in Q3
2025 card net charge-off rate guidance improved to approximately 3.3% from prior expectations on favorable delinquency trends driven by continued consumer resilience

risks.text: Wholesale charge-offs elevated due to apparent fraud in secured lending facilities, including $170M Tricolor charge-off; Jamie Dimon warned 'when you see one cockroach, there are probably more'
CET1 ratio declined 30 bps to 14.8% driven by higher RWA from wholesale lending growth across Banking and Markets
2026 NII ex-Markets preliminary view of ~$95B faces headwinds from rate cuts (75 bps in 2025 plus two 25 bps cuts expected in H1 2026) given asset-sensitive balance sheet

Deposit balance growth inflection point pushed out due to lower personal savings rate, robust consumer spending outpacing income, strong equity market flows, and higher-than-expected rates driving yield-seeking behavior

Management flagged potential for labor market deterioration and broader credit cycle, noting 'low-hiring, low-firing' dynamic reflects high employer uncertainty; Jamie Dimon warned NBFI/private credit losses could be 'a little bit worse than other people expect' in a downturn

guidance_items.detail: Q4 NII ex-Markets expected ~$23.5B; Q4 total NII expected ~$25B
Q4 adjusted expense ~$24.5B, implying FY $95.9B, up from prior guidance driven by stronger revenue environment
2025 card net charge-off rate now expected ~3.3%, improved from prior guidance on favorable delinquency trends
Preliminary 2026 NII ex-Markets central case ~$95B, subject to budget cycle completion and usual caveats
2026 consensus expense of ~$100B flagged as 'a little bit low', implying expenses will come in above Street estimates

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: NBFI/non-bank financial institution lending exposure and credit risk, including Tricolor fraud and broader private credit underwriting standards
